en.greeting: Welcome back! Today we use numbers for time: days, months, clock times and dates. Let's take it one step at a time.

steps.title: Days of the week
steps.text: Let's start with the seven days.
steps.body: Every day starts with a **capital letter** and ends in **-day**. Use **on** with days: **on Monday**, **on Friday**. Not 'in Monday'. Wednesday sounds like **WENZ-day** — the first d is silent.

steps.title: Months of the year
steps.text: Now the twelve months. Many look like Indonesian!
steps.body: Months also start with a **capital letter**. Use **in** with months: **in May**, **in December**. Not 'on May'. Watch the ones that change most: Mei → **May**, Juni → **June**, Juli → **July**, Agustus → **August**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Is it a day or a month? That tells you the little word.

question.explanation: Saturday is a day, and days take **on**: on Saturday. **In** is for months (in May) and **at** is for clock times (at seven o'clock).

steps.title: What time is it?
steps.text: Now let's read the clock.
steps.body: Answer with **It's** + the time. Full hours: **o'clock**. **past** = after the hour, **to** = before the next hour. Big warning: Indonesian 'setengah sebelas' is 10:30 = **half past ten**. Indonesian counts towards the next hour; English counts from the hour you just passed. The easy way: just say the numbers, **ten thirty**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Think in English: which hour did the clock just pass?

question.prompt: Rina finishes work at 'setengah enam' (5:30). How do you say the time?
question.explanation: 5:30 is half an hour **past five**, so **half past five** (or **five thirty**). 'Setengah enam' counts towards six, but English counts from five. 'Half six' means 6:30 in British English.

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: Press play. Listen for past or to.

question.prompt: Listen. What time is the train?
question.listen: The train is at quarter past four.
question.explanation: **Quarter past four** = 15 minutes after four = 4:15. 4:45 would be **quarter to five**, and 3:45 is **quarter to four**.

steps.title: first, second, third…
steps.text: Dates need a special kind of number.
steps.body: Dates use **ordinal numbers**: say **the first of May** (or **May the first**), never 'the one of May'. Most ordinals just add **-th**: fourth, sixth, tenth. The special ones are **first, second, third, fifth, eighth, ninth, twelfth, twentieth**. Use **on** with dates.

steps.title: Dates in the year
steps.text: Here are some dates you know. Read them out loud.

examples.en: Independence Day is on the seventeenth of August.
Kartini Day is on the twenty-first of April.
My birthday is on the fifth of June.
The exam is on the thirtieth of November.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dates need an ordinal. Which one is 3?

question.prompt: How do you say the date 3 July?
question.explanation: Dates use ordinals: 3 → **third**, so **the third of July**. 'The three of July' uses a normal number, and **thirtieth** is 30th.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Put the words in order: on + the + ordinal + of + month.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Ulang tahun saya tanggal 2 Mei.
question.solution: My birthday is on the second of May.
question.explanation: Start with **My birthday is**, then **on** for a date, then **the second of May**. 2 becomes the ordinal **second**, not 'two'.

id.greeting: Selamat datang kembali! Hari ini kita memakai angka untuk waktu: hari, bulan, jam, dan tanggal. Yuk, satu langkah demi satu langkah.

steps.title: Nama hari
steps.text: Kita mulai dari tujuh nama hari.
steps.body: Setiap nama hari diawali **huruf kapital** dan berakhiran **-day**. Pakai **on** untuk hari: **on Monday**, **on Friday**. Bukan 'in Monday'. Wednesday dibaca **WENZ-day** — huruf d pertama tidak dibunyikan.

steps.title: Nama bulan
steps.text: Sekarang dua belas nama bulan. Banyak yang mirip bahasa Indonesia!
steps.body: Nama bulan juga diawali **huruf kapital**. Pakai **in** untuk bulan: **in May**, **in December**. Bukan 'on May'. Perhatikan yang paling berbeda: Mei → **May**, Juni → **June**, Juli → **July**, Agustus → **August**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Ini hari atau bulan? Dari situ kamu tahu kata kecilnya.

question.explanation: Saturday adalah nama hari, dan hari memakai **on**: on Saturday. **In** untuk bulan (in May) dan **at** untuk jam (at seven o'clock).

steps.title: Jam berapa?
steps.text: Sekarang kita belajar membaca jam.
steps.body: Jawab dengan **It's** + jamnya. Jam tepat: **o'clock**. **past** = lewat dari jam itu, **to** = kurang dari jam berikutnya. Awas: 'setengah sebelas' itu 10:30 = **half past ten**. Bahasa Indonesia menghitung menuju jam berikutnya; bahasa Inggris menghitung dari jam yang baru lewat. Cara mudah: sebut saja angkanya, **ten thirty**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Berpikirlah dalam bahasa Inggris: jam berapa yang baru saja lewat?

question.prompt: Rina selesai kerja jam setengah enam (5:30). Bagaimana mengucapkan jamnya?
question.explanation: 5:30 itu setengah jam **lewat jam lima**, jadi **half past five** (atau **five thirty**). 'Setengah enam' menghitung menuju jam enam, tapi bahasa Inggris menghitung dari jam lima. 'Half six' berarti 6:30 dalam bahasa Inggris British.

steps.title: Dengarkan
steps.text: Tekan putar. Dengarkan kata past atau to.

question.listen: The train is at quarter past four.
question.explanation: **Quarter past four** = 15 menit lewat jam empat = 4:15. 4:45 adalah **quarter to five**, dan 3:45 adalah **quarter to four**.

steps.title: first, second, third…
steps.text: Tanggal butuh jenis angka yang khusus.
steps.body: Tanggal memakai **bilangan urutan**: katakan **the first of May** (atau **May the first**), jangan 'the one of May'. Sebagian besar cukup ditambah **-th**: fourth, sixth, tenth. Yang khusus: **first, second, third, fifth, eighth, ninth, twelfth, twentieth**. Pakai **on** untuk tanggal.

steps.title: Tanggal-tanggal dalam setahun
steps.text: Ini beberapa tanggal yang kamu kenal. Bacakan dengan suara keras.

examples.en: Independence Day is on the seventeenth of August.
Kartini Day is on the twenty-first of April.
My birthday is on the fifth of June.
The exam is on the thirtieth of November.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Tanggal butuh bilangan urutan. Yang mana untuk 3?

question.explanation: Tanggal memakai bilangan urutan: 3 → **third**, jadi **the third of July**. 'The three of July' memakai angka biasa, dan **thirtieth** itu tanggal 30.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Susun kata-katanya: on + the + bilangan urutan + of + bulan.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Ulang tahun saya tanggal 2 Mei.
question.solution: My birthday is on the second of May.
question.explanation: Mulai dengan **My birthday is**, lalu **on** untuk tanggal, lalu **the second of May**. Angka 2 menjadi bilangan urutan **second**, bukan 'two'.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini ringkasan yang bisa kamu simpan dan buka lagi kapan saja.

tips: Setengah tujuh = 6:30 = **half past six**, bukan 'half seven'.
Tanggal memakai bilangan urutan: **the first of May**, bukan 'the one of May'.

The meeting is on Monday at nine o'clock.
